items.title: A24's Elden Ring movie reportedly costs $200 million, almost as much as a Marvel blockbuster
The 10 Greatest Video Game Masterpieces of the Last 10 Years, Ranked
items.summary: The last decade of gaming has produced a few truly masterful titles, many of which are already classics of the medium, from Elden Ring to Dead Space.
items.content:
Image via Team Cherry Add Collider on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Dawson Nyffenegger Published Oct 26, 2026, 4:48 PM EDT Sign in to your Collider account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap The last 10 years have seen a ton of amazing entries come out in the gaming world. From horror to shooters, every genre has had loads of incredible games come out from both indie and AAA developers. Some are exclusive to one platform, while others have attracted a wider audience by expanding to numerous platforms, but all have made gaming history as some of the greatest ever made.

It's honestly kind of hard to keep track of them all. While one could easily assemble a list of hundreds of video games that have come out since 2016 that can all be considered masterpieces, alas, there can only be ten. These are the most entertaining and most perfect video game masterpieces released over the last decade . They're all beloved pieces of gaming history, and yet this list is only scratching the surface of how many there truly are.

Battlefield 1 Rupture map Image via EA It's not very often that a first-person shooter franchise really knocks it out of the park, but DICE struck gold when they released Battlefield 1 . This FPS, contrary to many other entries in the genre, is set during the First World War . The campaign lets players step into the shoes of five different protagonists in five distinct areas of war. Players can fly high or drive a tank across the Western Front, scale the slopes of Monte Grappa, storm the beaches of Gallipoli, and ride with Lawrence of Arabia .

Of course, that isn't the only thing the game has to offer. It also features the franchise's iconic multiplayer mode, which includes massive battles of 64 players. You aren't strictly relegated to infantry roles, either. You can assume command of boats, ground vehicles, and planes , as well as use several historically accurate pieces of heavy artillery and machine guns. Better yet, the environments are fully destructible, adding to the immersion. This game really shows how hellish World War I was , yet it's also strangely beautiful sometimes. Battlefield 1 is something that every first-person shooter should aspire to be.

Image via Team Cherry Hollow Knight was a game that took everybody by surprise. At the time, there wasn't a lot of hope for it — it just seemed like another 2D side-scrolling adventure. However, when it came out, it completely blew all other games out of the water. In this role-playing Metroidvania , you play as a Hollow, a faceless insectoid creature exploring the broken world of Hallownest. Everything is shrouded in darkness, and pretty much every life form is reminiscent of some sort of insect.

This game stands out in its unparalleled atmosphere and unique vibe . It's not easy to compare to other games because there's just nothing else out there like it. Moreover, exploration was fun and rewarding, the boss fights are insanely creative, and there's no shortage of things to do. While Hollow Knight is a hard game, as many Metroidvanias are, it's still a necessary and exceptional experience for any video game fan.

A figure wearing a space suit in Dead Space Image via Motive Studios The 2023 remake of Dead Space is honestly more of a remaster. While it is technically a ground-up remake, it doesn't change much of anything about the gameplay or the level design. Regardless, it was great to revisit this horror masterpiece in a whole new way . This legendary piece of survival horror is about Isaac Clarke, a space miner who docks with a space station orbiting an alien planet, only to find that a parasitic life form has wiped out the entire mining crew.

Using a variety of unique weapons at your disposal, Isaac must navigate the mining station, determine the source of the outbreak, and rescue his girlfriend, who is also somewhere aboard. Thrown in with the long corridors are open, zero-gravity environments, where players can literally bounce off the walls or walk on the ceiling, both to give them an edge during combat and to open up new routes. Clarke is also equipped with a stasis device, allowing him to freeze aliens and move objects around like he has telekinesis. Mechanically, the original version of Dead Space was revolutionary, and the remake only improved that reputation .

Link in The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild Image via Nintendo The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild was the first new entry in the long-running RPG series to come out on Nintendo Switch, which meant the company really had to step it up. The result is this game, which isn't the best in the franchise, but it is certainly up there. The games have always been pretty open-ended and encouraged exploration, but this one really turned the land of Hyrule into a sandbox where players can do as they please.

The map is much larger than anything the franchise previously attempted, and there are tons of side activities to tackle. The game allows players to go at their own pace as they take Link on a journey to once again save the kingdom from the evil god Ganon. There are so many fresh and niche mechanics that got added into the game that it's hard to find any other series with a similar vibe. Already a modern classic, Breath of the Wild will likely be remembered alongside franchise greats like Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask .

Four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

You want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

You would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

items.title: ‘Elden Ring’ could become A24’s most expensive movie ever with a reported $200 million budget
items.summary: A24 allocates a record $200M budget for Alex Garland's Elden Ring film adaptation. Discover the cast, IMAX plans, and March 3, 2028 release date.
items.content:
Alex Garland’s adaptation marks a major departure from the studio’s usual spending.

The production company A24 is known for two things: the high quality of its films and the low budgets it has worked with. But some of that is about to change with its first video game adaptation, ‘Elden Ring’ .

According to a report in The Wall Street Journal, the next film directed by Alex Garland (‘Civil War,’ ‘Ex Machina’) will cost about $200 million , far exceeding what A24 had previously spent on other films. For context, the most expensive film to date had been ‘Marty Supreme,’ which cost $70 million, as well as ‘Civil War,’ which cost $50 million.

Based on the world developed by FromSoftware , with lore written by George R. R. Martin and winner of the 2022 Game of the Year award, ‘Elden Ring’ has a combination that, on paper, sounds like a winner. Production on the film has been underway for several months now, and from what we’ve learned about its development, it aims to be a faithful adaptation of the video game. The film features a cast full of familiar names, including Kit Connor, Ben Whishaw, Cailee Spaeny, Tom Burke, Havana Rose Liu, Sonoya Mizuno, Jonathan Pryce, and Nick Offerman . The film is being shot for IMAX , though it will take some time to reach theaters, with a release date set for March 3, 2028 .

It’s worth noting that this isn’t the only video game-related film A24 is currently working on. An adaptation of Death Stranding is currently in pre-production, and the production team has recently been scouting locations to bring this strange world—born from the mind of Hideo Kojima—to life.

items.title: The Elden Ring movie is reportedly A24’s most expensive production ever, with a budget of nearly $200 million
items.summary: A24 is going all in on Elden Ring. According to a new Wall Street Journal report, the studio’s live-action adaptation of FromSoftware’s hit RPG has ... Read more
items.content:
A24 is going all in on Elden Ring. According to a new Wall Street Journal report, the studio’s live-action adaptation of FromSoftware’s hit RPG has a budget of nearly $200 million. That makes it the most expensive film A24 has ever made, by a long way.

The figure reportedly comes from unnamed insiders and doesn’t include marketing. Earlier reports had put the budget at closer to $100 million, so it looks like the project has grown considerably.

A24 is known for smaller, director-driven films, so $200 million is a big jump. Its previous record was Marty Supreme, starring Timothée Chalamet, which cost around $70 million. Before that, Alex Garland’s Civil War held the title at around $50 million.

Garland is back with A24 for Elden Ring, writing and directing the film. Heartstopper star Kit Connor leads the cast, and George R.R. Martin, who helped create the game’s world and lore, is on board as a producer.

Filming wrapped earlier this summer after a shoot of around 100 days, and the movie is set to hit cinemas on March 3, 2028.

It’s easy to see why A24 is willing to spend so much. Elden Ring was a major hit when it launched in 2022, and analysts estimate it has sold over 36 million copies and brought in more than $2 billion in revenue. The game’s vast world, brutal bosses and mysterious lore make it a natural fit for a big-budget fantasy epic.

It’s still a risk, though. Video game adaptations have a mixed track record, and a $200 million budget plus marketing costs means the film will need to do serious business at the box office to make a profit. Fans will also be watching to see whether a story built on cryptic item descriptions and environmental storytelling can work as a two-hour movie.

With Garland in charge and Martin involved, there’s reason to be optimistic. But in the end, Elden Ring still has to be a good film.

items.title: ELDEN RING Movie Reportedly Has a Massive $200 Million Budget From A24
items.summary: A24 is spending some serious money to bring Elden Ring to the big screen, and it sounds like the studio is going all in on Alex Garland
items.content:
A24 is spending some serious money to bring Elden Ring to the big screen, and it sounds like the studio is going all in on Alex Garland's upcoming fantasy epic.

According to a report from The Wall Street Journal , the Elden Ring movie budget is approaching a whopping $200 million, making it the most expensive film A24 has ever backed.

That's a huge investment for a studio that built its reputation on smaller independent films, and it shows just how much confidence A24 has in this adaptation.

For comparison, A24's previous biggest production was Marty Supreme , starring Timothée Chalamet , which cost around $70 million and earned $191 million worldwide. The studio is now preparing to spend nearly three times that amount to bring FromSoftware's fantasy world to life.

Anyone who's played Elden Ring knows exactly why this movie could cost a fortune. The Lands Between are filled with towering castles, terrifying monsters, dragons, warring demigods, and some of the most incredible fantasy environments ever created for a video game. Then there's the massive Erdtree looming over everything.

Recreating that world for a live-action movie is going to require some serious resources, especially if Garland wants to capture the scale and atmosphere that made the game such an unforgettable experience.

The movie also has some impressive creative talent involved. George R.R. Martin , who created Game of Thrones , helped develop the game's mythology and backstory alongside FromSoftware director Hidetaka Miyazaki . Martin is also serving as a producer on the film, which is encouraging considering how important the lore is to the overall experience.

This massive investment is part of A24's larger push into blockbuster filmmaking. The studio raised $225 million in funding in 2022, followed by another investment round led by Josh Kushner's Thrive Capital in 2024, which helped push its valuation to $3.5 billion.

More recently, Google invested approximately $75 million in A24 through a partnership involving AI filmmaking tools. With that kind of financial backing, the studio has more freedom to take on expensive projects that would've been difficult to imagine during its early years.

Of course, throwing $200 million at a video game movie doesn't guarantee a hit.

Adapting a popular fantasy game comes with some serious financial risks. Having an established fanbase helps, but the movie still needs to deliver something that appeals to audiences beyond the people who've spent hundreds of hours playing the games.

A24 also has some experience with fantasy films that didn't exactly dominate the box office. David Lowery's The Green Knight offered a fascinating and unconventional take on Arthurian mythology, while Alex Scharfman's Death of a Unicorn mixed mythical creatures with a twisted story about corporate greed.

Neither film became a major theatrical success, although both found audiences through streaming. That kind of release strategy can work for smaller productions, but a $200 million movie needs a much bigger theatrical performance to justify its cost.

Personally, I'm incredibly excited about Elden Ring . It's one of those video game worlds that feels perfect for an ambitious fantasy movie, provided the filmmakers understand what makes it special.

items.title: A24's Elden Ring Live-Action Will Become the Studio's Most Expensive Movie Ever
items.summary: It's about to be almost 3 times more expensive than A24's biggest splurge to date, Marty Supreme.
items.content:
It's about to be almost 3 times more expensive than A24's biggest splurge to date, Marty Supreme.

Alex Garland's live-action adaptation of the world's beloved ARPG is about to become A24's most expensive production ever. It surpasses A24's budget for its current most costly title, Marty Supreme, by over $100 million. The estimated spending for Elden Ring stands at $200 million, compared to a humble $70 million for Marty Supreme. This also makes the upcoming movie Garland's most expensive directorial project, with Civil War's $50 million looking like a small, cost-efficient production.

Elden Ring, developed by FromSoftware, came out in 2022. The game was a massive success, becoming the most-awarded title in the Game of the Year category. It received the title over 300 times, making it Game of the Year according to D.I.C.E. Awards, Game Developers Choice Awards, The Steam Awards, and others. Its 2025 spin-off, Nightreign, saw humbler numbers and fewer awards, and still, it sold 2 million copies in 24 hours and gathered tens of thousands of Steam reviews that stand at 'Very positive.'

What we know about the Elden Ring movie so far is that the cast includes Nick Offerman, Emma Laird, Tom Burke, Jonathan Pryce, Cailee Spaeny, and Ben Whishaw. Vince Gerardis, Andrew Macdonald, George R.R. Martin, Matthew Penry-Davey, Allon Reich, and Peter Rice are credited as movie producers. VFX are being carried out under the supervision of Jörundur Rafn Arnarson.

While principal photography started in the United Kingdom and the crew filmed in England, Scotland, and Wales, some scenes were shot in Iceland. Confirmed filming locations for Elden Ring include Dinorwic Quarry, Dolbadarn Castle, and Conwy Castle.

The movie is set to come out on March 3, 2028. Its mind-blowing budget, estimated by WSJ , might grow bigger during post-production, and we'll get the final price for A24's epic dark fantasy closer to the release date. items.title: Elden Ring Movie Is Reportedly A $200 Million Gamble For A24
The Elden Ring Movie Will Be So Expensive That It’s Already Breaking Records
items.summary: A24’s upcoming production is shaping up to make history.
items.content:
The days when video game adaptations were considered doomed to fail on the big and small screens are long gone. Production companies are increasingly interested in video game franchises and are willing to invest heavily in bringing them to life. The upcoming Elden Ring movie is a perfect example, as it could already be breaking records before its release.

As fans of FromSoftware’s work will remember, Elden Ring conquered the video game world after a lengthy development process. Now, the acclaimed fantasy franchise is heading to the big screen with A24, the studio behind films such as Moonlight and Everything Everywhere All at Once .

Production on the live-action Elden Ring movie is reportedly progressing well, and new information suggests that A24 is putting considerable trust—and money—into the project. According to a report from The Wall Street Journal, cited by ComicBook, the film could have a budget of approximately $200 million USD.

For context, A24’s upcoming Backrooms movie reportedly cost $10 million USD to make, while its most expensive production to date is Marty Supreme , released in 2025 with a budget estimated at between $60 million and $70 million USD.

In other words, A24 could be spending more than three times as much on Bandai Namco Entertainment’s fantasy franchise, making Elden Ring the most expensive movie the studio has ever produced.

But that’s not all. If the reported budget is accurate, the project would not only become the biggest production in the New York-based studio’s history but also the most expensive video game movie ever made.

The current record holder is Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time , released in 2010, which had an estimated production budget of between $185 million and $200 million USD. Other major adaptations, including Warcraft , A Minecraft Movie , and Pokémon: Detective Pikachu , had budgets of around $160 million USD.

A24 began in 2012 as a film company focused on lower-budget productions, but its recent successes have attracted investor interest. That has allowed the studio to finance increasingly ambitious projects and even expand into video games.

In fact, Elden Ring won’t be A24’s first movie adaptation of a video game franchise. The studio is also behind Backrooms , which enjoyed tremendous success earlier this year, and it is the same company producing the film adaptation of Death Stranding .

Although spending this much money on a video game adaptation is unusual—especially for a relatively new franchise—A24 isn’t approaching the project blindly. Elden Ring has already proven its commercial success in the video game market, and the studio is well aware of the franchise’s potential, partly thanks to the involvement of George R. R. Martin, the author behind the hugely popular A Song of Ice and Fire saga.

There are reasons to believe the franchise could find a similarly enthusiastic audience in theaters. However, investing so much money in a single project still carries considerable risk, and it will be interesting to see whether the movie can replicate the success of the game or other A24 productions, such as Backrooms .

items.title: A24’s Elden Ring Movie Costs Nearly $200 Million
items.summary: A24’s Elden Ring adaptation is reportedly its most expensive film to date, with a nearly $200 million budget and a planned 2028 release.
items.content:
A24’s Elden Ring adaptation is reportedly its most expensive film to date, with a nearly $200 million budget and a planned 2028 release. A24’s previous most expensive release was Marty Supreme, with a budget of around $70 million, which surpassed the previous leader, Civil War, with a budget of about $50 million.

The relatively new FromSoftware franchise is seeing a quick turnaround in its screen adaptation. The game launched in February 2022 and features world-building courtesy of George R. R. Martin. To date, the game has sold over 36 million copies across Steam, PlayStation, and XBOX, and it’s known for its challenging gameplay.

The movie has a March 3, 2028 release date, and a new Wall Street Journal report says it will cost around $200 million to make. The report highlighted how A24 has become a major player in the film industry, with many now trying to copy its formula.

Major studios, meanwhile, are increasingly trying to copy the A24 playbook. Online horror properties that seem like they could become the next “Backrooms” have sparked multimillion-dollar bidding wars. Universal is backing a big-budget movie from the “Everything Everywhere” directors. “They’re a Goldilocks company. Just the right amount of people doing just the right amount of things,” said Julie Huntsinger, the Telluride director.

According to The Hollywood Reporter , Alex Garland will write and direct the movie, the same person who wrote and directed Civil War. The cast includes Kit Connor, Tom Burke, Rose Liu, and Nick Offerman , among others. The film is also expected to take about 100 days of principal photography.

items.title: PC users get dose of PS1 nostalgia with free Elden Ring meets Resident Evil taster
items.content:
Gamers nostalgic for something that resembles the early PlayStation days should look no further than False Oath.

Resident Evil fans are going to love this new PC exclusive, as it’s exactly what we’d imagine a game like Elden Ring would look like had it launched for the OG PlayStation.

As a console player, I’m horrendously jealous of the PC users, now more than ever after seeing the rumoured price for Xbox Project Helix .

Video game graphics are constantly improving and as such, the price of hardware is skyrocketing. Part of me wishes I’d just caved and bought a PC back in the day.

I’m even more jealous of PC users though after trying the False Oath demo on my Steam Deck.

Developed by Daniel Almenara and Nytelynn, False Oath is an upcoming Steam game that pays homage to PS1 games like Resident Evil , Dino Crisis, and more.

The synopsis reads: “ False Oath is a retro-style survival horror game set in a medieval era. A deadly plague spreads across the kingdom. Search for a cure before it’s too late.”

After looking at the screenshots and gameplay footage, you can tell the FromSoftware vibes are strong with this one. It’s very Kings Field -esque, but it’s exactly the type of game I’d picture in my head if you told me to imagine the likes of Elden Ring , Dark Souls or Demon Souls as a PS1 game.

It’s got a retro eeriness I haven’t seen since Crow Country , and it stands out from other games in the genre. I’m honestly surprised the idea hasn’t been done sooner.

False Oath is due to launch in Q1 of 2027 exclusively for PCs, but in the meantime, you can play a free demo to get a taste of what’s to come.

Despite Steam yielding no answer on whether the demo would work on Steam Deck, I threw caution to the wind and gave it a go anyway.

It didn’t work flawlessly, but it did the trick for some first impressions of the story, world design, and general gameplay. Hopefully when the full-game releases, it’ll be optimised for the Steam Deck.

From my own experience, I’d confidently say this is a game for me, and again that’s speaking as a huge fan of both Resident Evil and FromSoftware games. This scratches my itch for more modernised retro throwbacks .

It has that authentic clunkiness you’d expect from a game like this, and if the visuals weren’t so crisp, I’d have been fully convinced that this was some sort of long-lost PS1 game.

items.title: Elden Ring: Only 23.9% Finish It vs 36% Median [2026]
items.summary: Only 23.9% of players finish Elden Ring, far below the 36% median. See where players quit, how it compares, and what the 2026 data shows.
items.content:
Elden Ring players are finishing the game at rates that look high at first glance, but the hard numbers tell a more mixed story. Steam’s global achievement statistics list 23.9% of owners with the Elden Lord achievement and 10.4% with all 42 achievements. Those are the cleanest figures in circulation on October 23, 2026, and they now anchor a viral claim that Elden Ring fans are built different .

Elden Ring Completion Rate: The Verified Numbers What Steam’s Achievement Data Actually Measures The Funnel From Roundtable Hold to Elden Lord Where Players Leave: Reading the Drop-Offs The early game holds its audience The mid-game and late-game cliffs Testing the Built-Different Claim The 19-Game Comparison and Its 36% Median The 40% Figure Nobody Can Source What HowLongToBeat Adds: 60 Hours Versus 136 Fanatical’s 34.89% and 42.13%: Different Labels, Different Games Why Completion Statistics Mislead Market Impact: Why Publishers Care About Finish Rates Historical Context: How Completion Became a Scoreboard Competitive Comparison: Elden Ring Against the Pack Predictions: What Happens Next The Takeaway FAQ What percentage of players have beaten Elden Ring? How many players earn all 42 Elden Ring achievements? Is the Elden Ring completion rate higher than most games? Is it true that 40% of players beat the final boss? Which Elden Ring boss achievement has the lowest completion rate? How long does Elden Ring take to finish? What do Fanatical’s Beat It and Conquered It numbers mean? Are Elden Ring fans really built different? Related Coverage FRVR is among the outlets running the story, which pitches the Elden Ring completion rate as higher than most other games. The data does not fully back that framing. One comparison of 19 single-player games reports an ending-achievement rate of about 24% for Elden Ring against a median of about 36% for the whole set. That puts the game about 12 points below the middle of that pack, not above it.

This analysis sorts out what each figure measures, where the numbers stop and speculation starts, and what the debate says about how the industry reads completion data. For a sense of the audience behind these percentages, our coverage of the Steam hardware and software survey shows how large and varied the Steam player base is.

The week's biggest stories in tech, gaming and security, in one email.

Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google

Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.

Before any argument about who is built different, it helps to separate what is confirmed from what is repeated. The fact base for this story is narrow, and every figure below traces to a named source. Where a claim lacks a method, a date, or a platform, this article says so and keeps it out of the main analysis.

Three claims fail the same test. The headline idea that Elden Ring fans are built different has no measurable definition. The statement that roughly 40% of players have beaten the final boss comes with no method, platform, date, or source in the available material. And the broad line that the game’s completion rate beats most other games rests on a single comparison set that does not support it on the ending metric.

Steam’s global achievement page reports the share of all owners who have unlocked each achievement. That denominator matters. It counts everyone who bought the game, including people who never launched it, people who played an hour and drifted away, and people who own it only because it sat in a bundle or a sale. A completion rate built on owners will always read lower than one built on active players.

So when Steam lists 23.9% for Elden Lord, the plain reading is that just under one in four owners has earned that achievement. It does not say that 23.9% of people who seriously tried the game reached that point. The true rate among committed players is higher, but no available source quantifies it. Anyone quoting a higher number without naming the denominator is guessing.

The same logic applies to the 10.4% figure for all 42 achievements. A full-achievement run asks for far more than a story finish, so it works as a ceiling on dedication rather than a measure of ordinary completion. Roughly one owner in ten has cleared every item on the list, which is a meaningful number for a long game with a reputation for punishment, but it is not proof of a unique fan base.

Steam’s per-achievement percentages let us build a rough funnel. The table below orders the confirmed figures from highest to lowest and adds two derived columns. The first shows the points lost against the row above, and the second shows what share of the previous row’s players kept going. Note that the order reflects the percentages, not a guaranteed play sequence, since players can tackle some bosses in a different order.

Source: Steam global achievement statistics for Elden Ring. Derived columns are this site’s arithmetic on the listed percentages.

The first two steps lose very little. Going from Roundtable Hold at 75.0% to Margit, the Fell Omen at 71.0% costs 4 points, and Shardbearer Godrick at 65.1% costs another 5.9. About 94.7% and 91.7% of the previous group carried on. For a game with a hard reputation, that is a sticky opening. One in four owners never reaches Roundtable Hold at all, which may point to a pool of buyers who barely started.

Expand Your Collection

Each of these officially licensed mini replicas has been crafted by Pure Arts to faithfully capture the spirit, craftsmanship, and legendary designs of the Elden Ring universe. items.title: Patch Notes Version 1.17
items.summary: Patch 1.17 has been released for ELDEN RING . This patch aims to bring support the Tarnished Pack DLC , scheduled for release on Friday, August 28, 2026 , and to implement gameplay balance adjustments. Please apply the latest update before
items.content:
Patch 1.17 has been released for ELDEN RING. This patch aims to bring support the Tarnished Pack DLC, scheduled for release on Friday, August 28, 2026, and to implement gameplay balance adjustments. Please apply the latest update before playing.

MAIN UPDATE ADDITIONS

Tarnished Pack Additional Content

The following elements will be added upon purchase of the "Tarnished Pack" DLC.

  • Added Idus Knight and Heavy Knight as new starting classes, selectable during character creation. Note: The equipment of each new starting class can also be obtained by purchasing it from merchants in the Lands Between or by finding it in the world.

    [/*]

  • Added weapons that can be purchased from merchants or found in the Lands Between.

    [/*]

  • Added three types of Spectral Steed Attire that change the appearance of Torrent: - Tree Sentinel Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Stormveil Castle. - Silver of Caria Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Liurnia of the Lakes. - Funereal Night Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Altus Plateau. Note: After obtaining any Spectral Steed Attire, the option to change the spectral steed’s appearance will be added to the Site of Grace menu.

    [/*]

  • Added an NPC invasion event in Caelid.

    [/*]

  • Added an NPC invasion event in Leyndell, Royal Capital. Note: This event will not occur after the area has changed to Leyndell, Ashen Capital.

    [/*]

The "Tarnished Pack" release times are as follows: Steam: Friday, August 28 at 7:00 JST | 00:00 CEST | 15:00 PDT.

Balance Adjustments

Changed certain items found in the field or obtained by defeating certain powerful enemies in the Realm of Shadow to higher-tier items or other treasures. Note: Items already that were already found will not be changed.

Weapons

  • Smithscript Dagger / Rellana's Twin Blades → Increased critical hit power.

    [/*]

  • Smithscript Axe / Smithscript Spear / Spear of the Impaler → Reduced the stamina consumption of weapon-throwing attacks. → Increased the power of weapon-throwing attacks.

    [/*]

  • Carian Sorcery Sword → Changed Intelligence scaling so that it now increases the attack power of all damage types.

    [/*]

  • Smithscript Greathammer → Increased the power of weapon-throwing attacks.

    [/*]

  • Golem Fist → Increased the range of the fist-launching heavy attack.

    [/*]

  • Firespark Perfume Bottle / Lightning Perfume Bottle / Chilling Perfume Bottle / Frenzyflame Perfume Bottle / Deadly Poison Perfume Bottle → Increased attack power.

    [/*]

  • Lordsworn's Shield / Briar Greatshield / Spiked Palisade Shield / Icon Shield / Golden Beast Crest Shield / Manor Towershield / Crossed-Tree Towershield / Inverted Hawk Towershield / Dragon Towershield / Distinguished Greatshield / Gilded Greatshield / Black Steel Greatshield / Ant's Skull Plate / Erdtree Greatshield → Increased guard boost. → Reduced weight.

    [/*]

  • Wooden Greatshield / Cuckoo Greatshield / Redmane Greatshield / Golden Greatshield / Crucible Hornshield / Dragonclaw Shield / Eclipse Crest Greatshield / Jellyfish Shield / One-Eyed Shield → Increased guard boost.

    [/*]

  • Haligtree Crest Greatshield → Reduced weight.

    [/*]

  • Rakshasa's Great Katana → Increased the time before an attack can be performed with a right-hand weapon immediately after attacking with this weapon equipped in the left hand.

    [/*]

Skills

  • Parry → Improved parry performance. → Reduced the time before various actions can be performed after activation when used with Daggers, Curved Swords, or Small Shields.

    [/*]

  • Storm Wall → Changed the skill so that it no longer consumes FP when used. → Improved parry performance.

    [/*]

  • Thops's Barrier → Improved parry performance.

    [/*]

Sorceries

  • Founding Rain of Stars → Increased power.

    [/*]

  • Carian Retaliation → Increased power.

    [/*]

  • Meteorite → Reduced casting time.

    [/*]

  • Meteorite of Astel → Reduced casting time.

    [/*]

  • Gravitational Missile → Changed the spell so that the gravity projectile does not explode immediately upon striking terrain such as the ground or a wall.

    [/*]

Incantations

  • Feather of the Divine Bird → Increased power.

    [/*]

  • O, Flame! → Expanded attack range.

    [/*]

  • Rain of Fire → Increased power.

    [/*]

PvP-Exclusive Balance Adjustments

Weapons

  • Rakshasa's Great Katana → Increased damage taken from attacks by other players while attacking.

    [/*]

Incantations

  • Rugalea's Roar → Reduced power against other players.

    [/*]

  • Rotten Breath / Ekzykes's Decay → Reduced the amount of time other player characters are unable to move from hit reactions when struck by these incantations.

    [/*]

Bug Fixes

Fixed a bug where critical hits dealt with Great Katana weapon types had lower-than-expected power against large enemies. Fixed a bug where jumping attacks with Great Katana weapon types could be parried.

PC-Only Bug Fixes

Fixed a bug that prevented camera control with the mouse during NPC dialogue when using keyboard and mouse controls Fixed a bug in the "Keyboard/Mouse Settings" section of the system menu in which selecting the reset option did not restore various settings to their defaults The version number shown in the lower-right corner of the title screen after applying this update will be as follows:

App Ver. 1.17 Regulation Ver. 1.17

This update is required for online play.

We will continue to make improvements so that you can enjoy ELDEN RING more comfortably. Thank you for your continued support.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stormveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.
